description: Labeled cases for bib_doctor.py — bibliography hygiene: DOI syntax and URL-prefix normalization, duplicate detection by DOI and by near-identical title, required fields per entry type, key style, and the verified={true} stamp that marks an entry as machine-fetched rather than remembered. The negatives are the entries that look defective and are not: a preprint that legitimately has no journal, an @misc carrying a url instead of a doi, an @inproceedings whose venue lives in booktitle, and two distinct papers whose titles share most of their words.

cases.comment: doi2bib writes a bare DOI; a hand-pasted one usually arrives as a resolver URL. Normalizable, so it reports a fix rather than just a complaint.
cases.bib:
@article{kaya2023deep,
  title = {Deep learning for bearing fault diagnosis},
  author = {Kaya, Ahmet},
  journal = {Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing},
  year = {2023},
  doi = {https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymssp.2023.00001},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: A string in the doi field that cannot resolve is worse than an empty one: it looks verified.
cases.bib:
@article{demir2022vibration,
  title = {Vibration analysis with wavelets},
  author = {Demir, Cem},
  journal = {Journal of Sound and Vibration},
  year = {2022},
  doi = {ymssp-2022-00042},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: The classic double-import: the same paper found in two databases, cited under two keys, counted twice in the reference list.
cases.bib:
@article{kaya2023deep,
  title = {Deep learning for bearing fault diagnosis},
  author = {Kaya, Ahmet},
  journal = {MSSP},
  year = {2023},
  doi = {10.1016/j.ymssp.2023.00001},
  verified = {true},
}

@article{kaya2023bearing,
  title = {Deep learning approaches to rolling bearing diagnosis},
  author = {Kaya, Ahmet},
  journal = {MSSP},
  year = {2023},
  doi = {10.1016/j.ymssp.2023.00001},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: The same paper imported twice without a DOI on either copy — only the title can catch it.
cases.bib:
@article{yilmaz2021survey,
  title = {A survey of deep learning for condition monitoring},
  author = {Yilmaz, Berk},
  journal = {IEEE Access},
  year = {2021},
  verified = {true},
}

@article{yilmaz2021review,
  title = {A survey of deep-learning for condition monitoring},
  author = {Yilmaz, Berk},
  journal = {IEEE Access},
  year = {2021},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: An @article with no journal is an entry that will render as a dangling reference in every citation style.
cases.bib:
@article{ozkan2020signal,
  title = {Signal preprocessing for fault detection},
  author = {Ozkan, Deniz},
  year = {2020},
  doi = {10.1109/access.2020.00002},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: Keys are renamed by hand because in-text [@key] would break otherwise, so this reports and never auto-fixes.
cases.bib:
@article{Kaya_2023_Deep,
  title = {Deep learning for bearing fault diagnosis},
  author = {Kaya, Ahmet},
  journal = {MSSP},
  year = {2023},
  doi = {10.1016/j.ymssp.2023.00001},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: No verified={true} means the entry did not come from DOI content negotiation. It may be perfectly correct — and there is no way to tell, which is the whole point of the stamp.
cases.bib:
@article{hatirlanan2019kayit,
  title = {A remembered reference},
  author = {Biri, Bir},
  journal = {Bir Dergi},
  year = {2019},
  doi = {10.1000/xyz123},
}

@article{kaya2023deep,
  title = {Deep learning for bearing fault diagnosis},
  author = {Kaya, Ahmet and Yilmaz, Berk},
  journal = {Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing},
  year = {2023},
  doi = {10.1016/j.ymssp.2023.00001},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: NEGATIVE, and the reason the preprint carve-out exists: doi.org types an arXiv DOI as @article, but a preprint has no peer-reviewed journal. Demanding one flags a perfectly valid, authoritatively-fetched entry.
cases.bib:
@article{arikan2024transformer,
  title = {Transformers for vibration signals},
  author = {Arikan, Ege},
  year = {2024},
  doi = {10.48550/arXiv.2401.00001},
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  eprint = {2401.00001},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: NEGATIVE. A dataset or standard has a locator, not a DOI; url|doi is satisfied by either.
NEGATIVE. A conference paper has no journal field by definition; requiring one per @article rules would flag every CS proceedings entry in the bibliography.
cases.bib:
@inproceedings{sahin2022cnn,
  title = {A CNN baseline for bearing faults},
  author = {Sahin, Ali},
  booktitle = {Proceedings of the International Conference on Condition Monitoring},
  year = {2022},
  doi = {10.1145/3477495.0000001},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: NEGATIVE. Two genuinely distinct papers from the same group. A title matcher tuned loosely enough to merge these would silently delete a real reference.
cases.bib:
@article{demir2022bearing,
  title = {Wavelet features for bearing fault detection},
  author = {Demir, Cem},
  journal = {JSV},
  year = {2022},
  doi = {10.1016/j.jsv.2022.00001},
  verified = {true},
}

@article{demir2023gearbox,
  title = {Wavelet features for gearbox fault detection},
  author = {Demir, Cem},
  journal = {JSV},
  year = {2023},
  doi = {10.1016/j.jsv.2023.00002},
  verified = {true},
}

cases.comment: NEGATIVE. A project before its first source is registered has no bibliography defects.

mutations.breaks: An @article with no journal, or any entry missing a required field, stops being reported — the entry renders as a dangling reference in the built manuscript.
replace: missing = [f for f in req if not fields.get(f)]

mutations.breaks: The same paper imported from two databases under two keys is counted twice in the reference list and cited as if it were two sources.
Every arXiv/bioRxiv entry is flagged for a missing journal it cannot have — a false positive on entries doi2bib.py fetched correctly, which is how a linter teaches its user to ignore it.
An entry that never went through DOI content negotiation stops being distinguishable from one that did — the zero-fabrication chain's last visible link.
A doi field holding a resolver URL is no longer normalized or reported, so the raw string reaches the bibliography and every downstream DOI comparison against it fails.
Drops the near-identical-title threshold from 95 to 55, so two distinct papers from the same group are reported as duplicates and a real reference gets deleted.
